display_name: Hemu, Bairam Khan & Akbar – Second Battle of Panipat
one_line: Three converging figures at Panipat in 1556: Hemu the Hindu general-king, Akbar the young Mughal emperor, and Bairam Khan the regent-commandant.

appearance.age_look: Hemu: late 40s, sturdy and broad-shouldered; Akbar: mid-teens, lean and athletic; Bairam Khan: early 50s, tall and imposing.
appearance.face: Hemu has a square face, wheatish complexion, trimmed moustache and short beard, calm but intense gaze; Akbar has an oval face, light brown complexion, soft yet determined eyes with a faint youthful smile; Bairam Khan has a long face, darker brown complexion, sharp aquiline nose, neatly groomed full beard and a stern, calculating expression.
appearance.hair: Hemu’s hair is black, shoulder-length, combed back and partly hidden by a deep-maroon padded turban with a simple gold band; Akbar’s hair is dark brown, shoulder-length, straight, tucked behind ears and framed by a light-green Mughal turban with a white sarpech plume; Bairam Khan’s hair is black, mostly hidden under a dark-blue conical Mughal turban with a narrow gold edge and no plume.
appearance.costume: Hemu wears over a quilted off-white cotton tunic a mustard-yellow steel breastplate with simple engraved borders, paired with deep-green padded sleeves, a maroon cloth sash tied at the waist, and loose off-white churidar trousers tucked into mid-calf brown leather riding boots, with a plain round steel shield slung on his back; Akbar wears a knee-length light-cream quilted jama (cross-over robe) with fine diagonal stitching and a wide dark-red sash, over which sits a polished light-bronze breastplate with minimal decoration, matched with olive-green churidar trousers, soft brown leather ankle boots, and a narrow dagger tucked into his sash; Bairam Khan wears a rich dark-blue velvet ankle-length jama with subtle gold floral motifs, belted with a broad maroon sash, over which he has a steel-plated coat-of-mail cuirass that covers chest and shoulders, paired with dark-brown churidar trousers and black leather riding boots, and a long dark-brown cloak draped from one shoulder for a commander’s presence.
appearance.signature: Hemu carries a long slightly-curved steel talwar with a plain brass hilt and a maroon scabbard; Akbar carries a slender straight steel sword with a simple cross-hilt and polished dark-brown scabbard; Bairam Khan carries a long curved steel talwar with an ornate gold-inlaid hilt and a deep-blue scabbard that matches his robe.

ref_desc: Hemu is a sturdy middle-aged commander in mustard-yellow breastplate, maroon turban and off-white quilted armour with a talwar; young Akbar is lean in cream quilted jama, light-bronze cuirass and green turban; Bairam Khan is tall in dark-blue velvet jama, mail cuirass and blue-sheathed talwar.
sheet_prompt: Draw three full-body anime-style figures from 1556 Panipat as a model sheet: first, Hemu, a sturdy late-40s general with a square face, wheatish complexion, trimmed moustache and short beard, black shoulder-length hair under a deep-maroon padded turban with a simple gold band, wearing an off-white quilted cotton tunic, mustard-yellow steel breastplate with simple engraved borders, deep-green padded sleeves, maroon cloth sash, loose off-white churidar trousers and brown leather riding boots, carrying a long slightly-curved steel talwar with a brass hilt and maroon scabbard and a plain round steel shield on his back; second, young Akbar, a lean mid-teen with an oval face, light brown complexion, determined eyes, dark brown shoulder-length hair and a light-green Mughal turban with a white plume, dressed in a knee-length light-cream quilted jama with diagonal stitching, wide dark-red sash, light-bronze breastplate, olive-green churidar trousers and soft brown ankle boots, bearing a slender straight steel sword with a simple cross-hilt in a dark-brown scabbard at his waist; third, Bairam Khan, a tall early-50s commander with a long face, darker brown complexion, sharp nose, full trimmed beard, black hair under a dark-blue conical turban with a narrow gold edge, wearing a rich dark-blue velvet ankle-length jama patterned with subtle gold floral motifs, broad maroon sash, steel-plated mail cuirass over the chest and shoulders, dark-brown churidar trousers, black leather riding boots and a long dark-brown cloak draped from one shoulder, carrying a long curved steel talwar with an ornate gold-inlaid hilt and deep-blue scabbard, all in a historically grounded North Indian mid-16th-century style with a palette of mustard yellow, deep maroon, dark blue, olive green and light cream.
